intro:
Howdy all! October is here, and so is a busy stretch for the ERC.

This Friday, Dr. Mark Hlavacik joins us for an EdTalk on his new book, *Willing Warriors*. On October 20, the ERC hosts a colloquium with three National Academy of Education members. Inside this issue, you will also find our new report tracing a decade of *iteach* candidates from application to classroom.

Thanks for reading!

callouts.title: Share something with the ERC
callouts.text: Research, an event, an announcement: if it belongs in the newsletter or on the Policy Exchange, send it our way. The ERC team reviews everything before it goes out.

fields.title: The Pipeline of Alternative Teacher Certification: Evaluating iteach
fields.authors: Andrew Kwok, Brendan Bartanen, Kate Barnes
fields.summary: Alternative certification now supplies most new Texas teachers, but evidence on how those teachers fare has been limited. This ERC study tracks a decade of *iteach* candidates in Texas, Virginia, and Louisiana, following who applies, enrolls, finishes, and stays teaching. The pipeline is expanding rapidly; Texas applications have tripled since 2015. Many join mid-career from other fields. Notably, five years in, *iteach* completers remain in classrooms at higher rates than their peers.

fields.title: ERC Colloquium: Controversies in the Classroom
fields.location: Texas A&M Hotel, Ross Room, College Station, TX
fields.summary:
Moderated by **Lori Taylor**

We invite you to join us as the ERC hosts a special colloquium with three National Academy of Education members (**Bob Pianta**, **Mark Berends**, and **Jinfa Cai**) addressing education’s most pressing issues. Drinks & hors d’oeuvres will be provided.

fields.title: ERC EdTalk with Mark Hlavacik
fields.summary: Dr. Mark Hlavacik discusses his new book, *Willing Warriors*, and how the culture wars have redefined the politics of U.S. schooling from the 1970s to today. Lunch and refreshments will be provided; please RSVP.
